title: Record pointer stack recycling
summary: Recover the thiscall transfer at VA 0x548b30: decrement source +0x20, read indexed 32-bit pointer token, store into owner +0x158 indexed by +0x168, then increment the destination count. Direct callers at 0x548768 and 0x5487cb pass owner +0x170. Preserve store/count overlap and leave popped entries intact.
test_description: Compare original and recovered complete owner/source storage across 225 combinations: source counts 1..9, destination counts 0..4, and five pointer patterns including null, high-bit and all-ones tokens. Independently assert expected writes and unchanged bytes. Exercise four consecutive LIFO transfers. Counts beyond inferred slot capacities are controlled in-object overlap probes, not claims of valid gameplay inputs.
known_limits: Original class names and semantic identities of surrounding fields remain unknown; four-slot banks are inferred from adjacent routine 0x548b60.
Null objects, empty-source underflow and indices outside supplied storage are unchecked in the original and are not executed; no safe error handling is invented.
32-bit pointer tokens preserve the original layout; a native 64-bit port needs an explicit address/ownership adaptation.
No return value contract is inferred from incidental EAX; no byte matching is claimed.
